scenario: Bought 1 Jul 2024 for 12,000, sold 1 Jul 2025 for 9,000; insurance 1 Apr 2024 to 30 Sep 2025 for 1,096, starting 91 days before the purchase and running 91 days past the sale
derivation: Spec 7.7: lines dated before the purchase date are outside the ownership period, and a document's ledger date is its start (1 Apr 2024), so since bought counts none of the 1,096. Running = the 500 fill-up alone (1 entry). Depreciation 12,000 - 9,000 = 3,000 over 12 months. Total 3,500.
Distance 10,000 mi = 16,093.44 km. Per km: running 500 / 16,093.44 = 0.031069; depreciation 3,000 / 16,093.44 = 0.186411; together 0.217480 = 0.35 a mile (running 0.050001, depreciation 0.299999).

Spec 7.35 (#564): the cover is 548 days (1 Apr 2024 to 30 Sep 2025) at 1,096, so 2 a day. Only the days inside the ownership count in a year: 1 Jul to 31 Dec 2024 = 184 days = 368; 1 Jan to 1 Jul 2025 = 182 days = 364. The 91 days before the purchase and the 91 days after the sale count nowhere.
So for this document the years (368 + 364 = 732) are more than since bought (0): its ledger date is outside the period although most of its cover is inside.

page: Total: £500.00 of running costs + £3,000.00 of depreciation = £3,500.00.
